title: Check if All A's Appears Before All B's
approach_name: Check that no a appears after the first b
notes:
Task and constraints: Return true if every a in the string occurs before every b.
Idea: `checkString` verifies the string never contains an `a` after a `b`, using a seen-`b` flag or checking that no `a` occurs after the first `b`.
Technique and why it applies: A single scan detects the only forbidden transition, from a `b` back to an `a`.
Invariant: Once a `b` has appeared, every later character must be `b`; encountering a later `a` invalidates the order.
Edge cases: All-a, all-b, and empty strings are valid when allowed; the string must not transition from b back to a.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity_reason: A single scan detects the only forbidden transition, from a `b` back to an `a`.

title: Check if All A's Appears Before All B's
approach_name: Check that no a appears after the first b
notes:
Task and constraints: Return true if every a in the string occurs before every b.
Idea: `checkString` verifies the string never contains an `a` after a `b`, using a seen-`b` flag or checking that no `a` occurs after the first `b`.
Technique and why it applies: A single scan detects the only forbidden transition, from a `b` back to an `a`.
Invariant: Once a `b` has appeared, every later character must be `b`; encountering a later `a` invalidates the order.
Edge cases: All-a, all-b, and empty strings are valid when allowed; the string must not transition from b back to a.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
code: class Solution { public boolean checkString(String s){boolean seenB=false;for(char c:s.toCharArray()){if(c=='b')seenB=true;else if(seenB)return false;}return true;} }
complexity_reason: A single scan detects the only forbidden transition, from a `b` back to an `a`.

title: Check if Every Row and Column Contains All Numbers
approach_name: Validate row and column permutations
notes:
Task and constraints: Return true if each row and each column of an n by n matrix contains every integer from 1 through n exactly once.
Idea: For each row and column, compare the distinct values against the required set `{1,...,n}` or check that each has exactly n distinct values.
Technique and why it applies: Checking distinct membership in every row and column verifies both permutation constraints.
Invariant: Each row and each column must contain every legal number exactly once, so no missing or duplicate value is permitted.
Edge cases: The matrix is n by n; values outside 1 through n invalidate the relevant row or column; duplicates fail even if all cells are filled.
Complexity: O(n²) time expected with sets or O(n³) if each row and column is checked naively; auxiliary space depends on the checking sets.
complexity_reason: Checking distinct membership in every row and column verifies both permutation constraints.

title: Check if Every Row and Column Contains All Numbers
approach_name: Validate row and column permutations
notes:
Task and constraints: Return true if each row and each column of an n by n matrix contains every integer from 1 through n exactly once.
Idea: For each row and column, compare the distinct values against the required set `{1,...,n}` or check that each has exactly n distinct values.
Technique and why it applies: Checking distinct membership in every row and column verifies both permutation constraints.
Invariant: Each row and each column must contain every legal number exactly once, so no missing or duplicate value is permitted.
Edge cases: The matrix is n by n; values outside 1 through n invalidate the relevant row or column; duplicates fail even if all cells are filled.
Complexity: O(n²) time expected with sets or O(n³) if each row and column is checked naively; auxiliary space depends on the checking sets.
code: class Solution { public boolean checkValid(int[][] matrix){int n=matrix.length;for(int i=0;i<n;i++){boolean[] row=new boolean[n+1],col=new boolean[n+1];for(int j=0;j<n;j++){int a=matrix[i][j],b=matrix[j][i];if(a<1||a>n||b<1||b>n||row[a]||col[b])return false;row[a]=true;col[b]=true;}}return true;} }
complexity_reason: Checking distinct membership in every row and column verifies both permutation constraints.

title: Minimum Cost of Buying Candies With Discount
approach_name: Sort prices and discount every third candy
notes:
Task and constraints: Buy all candies while every third candy in descending-price order is free. Return the minimum total cost.
Idea: Sort prices in descending order and sum all prices except indices `2,5,8,...`, which represent each third candy made free.
Technique and why it applies: Descending sorting places the cheapest item of each group of three at the free position.
Invariant: Within every consecutive group of three descending prices, the cheapest is the third, so making it free minimizes the cost.
Edge cases: Fewer than three candies have no free item; equal prices are interchangeable; every candy is purchased.
Complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space if sorting a copy is used.
complexity_reason: Descending sorting places the cheapest item of each group of three at the free position.

title: Minimum Cost of Buying Candies With Discount
approach_name: Sort prices and discount every third candy
notes:
Task and constraints: Buy all candies while every third candy in descending-price order is free. Return the minimum total cost.
Idea: Sort prices in descending order and sum all prices except indices `2,5,8,...`, which represent each third candy made free.
Technique and why it applies: Descending sorting places the cheapest item of each group of three at the free position.
Invariant: Within every consecutive group of three descending prices, the cheapest is the third, so making it free minimizes the cost.
Edge cases: Fewer than three candies have no free item; equal prices are interchangeable; every candy is purchased.
Complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space if sorting a copy is used.
code:
import java.util.*;
class Solution { public int minimumCost(int[] cost){Arrays.sort(cost);int sum=0;for(int i=0;i<cost.length;i++){int price=cost[cost.length-1-i];if(i%3!=2)sum+=price;}return sum;} }
complexity_reason: Descending sorting places the cheapest item of each group of three at the free position.

title: Minimum Sum of Four Digit Number After Splitting Digits
approach_name: Distribute sorted digits alternately
notes:
Task and constraints: Rearrange the four digits into two two-digit numbers with minimum possible sum.
Idea: Sort the four digits and distribute them alternately into the tens and ones positions of two numbers, then return their sum.
Technique and why it applies: Sorting the digits before balancing place values minimizes the sum of the two formed numbers.
Invariant: The smallest digits occupy the higher place values across both numbers, and alternating assignment balances the place-value contributions.
Edge cases: The input has exactly four digits; leading zero can make a two-digit arrangement numerically smaller; digits are reused only as supplied.
Complexity: O(1) time and O(1) space because there are exactly four digits.
complexity_reason: Sorting the digits before balancing place values minimizes the sum of the two formed numbers.

title: Minimum Sum of Four Digit Number After Splitting Digits
approach_name: Distribute sorted digits alternately
notes:
Task and constraints: Rearrange the four digits into two two-digit numbers with minimum possible sum.
Idea: Sort the four digits and distribute them alternately into the tens and ones positions of two numbers, then return their sum.
Technique and why it applies: Sorting the digits before balancing place values minimizes the sum of the two formed numbers.
Invariant: The smallest digits occupy the higher place values across both numbers, and alternating assignment balances the place-value contributions.
Edge cases: The input has exactly four digits; leading zero can make a two-digit arrangement numerically smaller; digits are reused only as supplied.
Complexity: O(1) time and O(1) space because there are exactly four digits.
code:
import java.util.*;
class Solution { public int minimumSum(int num){char[] a=Integer.toString(num).toCharArray();Arrays.sort(a);return (a[0]-'0')*10+(a[2]-'0')+(a[1]-'0')*10+(a[3]-'0');} }
complexity_reason: Sorting the digits before balancing place values minimizes the sum of the two formed numbers.

title: Count Operations to Obtain Zero
approach_name: Repeatedly subtract the smaller number
notes:
Task and constraints: Count operations of subtracting the smaller positive number from the larger until either becomes zero.
Idea: While both values are positive, subtract the smaller from the larger and increment `ops`; return the number of iterations.
Technique and why it applies: Repeatedly subtracting the smaller positive value follows the specified operation until one operand becomes zero.
Invariant: At every iteration the pair is updated by one permitted operation, and `ops` counts exactly the operations performed so far.
Edge cases: If either input is zero initially, the answer is zero; positive values eventually reach zero; the subtraction is from larger to smaller.
Complexity: O(a+b) worst-case time for repeated subtraction and O(1) space.
complexity_reason: Repeatedly subtracting the smaller positive value follows the specified operation until one operand becomes zero.

title: Count Operations to Obtain Zero
approach_name: Repeatedly subtract the smaller number
notes:
Task and constraints: Count operations of subtracting the smaller positive number from the larger until either becomes zero.
Idea: While both values are positive, subtract the smaller from the larger and increment `ops`; return the number of iterations.
Technique and why it applies: Repeatedly subtracting the smaller positive value follows the specified operation until one operand becomes zero.
Invariant: At every iteration the pair is updated by one permitted operation, and `ops` counts exactly the operations performed so far.
Edge cases: If either input is zero initially, the answer is zero; positive values eventually reach zero; the subtraction is from larger to smaller.
Complexity: O(a+b) worst-case time for repeated subtraction and O(1) space.
code: class Solution { public int countOperations(int num1,int num2){int n=0;while(num1>0&&num2>0){if(num1>=num2)num1-=num2;else num2-=num1;n++;}return n;} }
complexity_reason: Repeatedly subtracting the smaller positive value follows the specified operation until one operand becomes zero.

title: Count Equal and Divisible Pairs in an Array
approach_name: Check equal values and divisible index product
notes:
Task and constraints: Count pairs i<j for which nums[i]==nums[j] and i*j is divisible by k.
Idea: Enumerate all pairs `i < j` and increment the answer when `nums[i] == nums[j]` and `(i*j) % k == 0`.
Technique and why it applies: Checking both value equality and index-product divisibility directly matches the pair definition.
Invariant: The nested loops examine every valid index pair exactly once, so each qualifying pair contributes one count.
Edge cases: Indices must be distinct and ordered; k is positive; equal values alone are insufficient without the product divisibility condition.
Complexity: O(n²) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity_reason: Checking both value equality and index-product divisibility directly matches the pair definition.

title: Count Equal and Divisible Pairs in an Array
approach_name: Check equal values and divisible index product
notes:
Task and constraints: Count pairs i<j for which nums[i]==nums[j] and i*j is divisible by k.
Idea: Enumerate all pairs `i < j` and increment the answer when `nums[i] == nums[j]` and `(i*j) % k == 0`.
Technique and why it applies: Checking both value equality and index-product divisibility directly matches the pair definition.
Invariant: The nested loops examine every valid index pair exactly once, so each qualifying pair contributes one count.
Edge cases: Indices must be distinct and ordered; k is positive; equal values alone are insufficient without the product divisibility condition.
Complexity: O(n²) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
code: class Solution { public int countPairs(int[] nums,int k){int ans=0;for(int i=0;i<nums.length;i++)for(int j=i+1;j<nums.length;j++)if(nums[i]==nums[j]&&(i*j)%k==0)ans++;return ans;} }
complexity_reason: Checking both value equality and index-product divisibility directly matches the pair definition.

title: Count Integers With Even Digit Sum
approach_name: Count values with even digit sum
notes:
Task and constraints: Count positive integers from 1 through num whose decimal digit sum is even.
Idea: Iterate integers from 1 through `num`, sum each integer's decimal digits using `% 10` and integer division, and count even digit sums.
Technique and why it applies: Extracting each decimal digit computes the exact digit sum whose parity determines whether the number is counted.
Invariant: For each candidate, the digit accumulator equals the sum of its processed decimal digits before its parity is tested.
Edge cases: The range starts at one and includes `num`; a single-digit number is handled by the same digit loop.
Complexity: O(num log num) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity_reason: Extracting each decimal digit computes the exact digit sum whose parity determines whether the number is counted.

title: Count Integers With Even Digit Sum
approach_name: Count values with even digit sum
notes:
Task and constraints: Count positive integers from 1 through num whose decimal digit sum is even.
Idea: Iterate integers from 1 through `num`, sum each integer's decimal digits using `% 10` and integer division, and count even digit sums.
Technique and why it applies: Extracting each decimal digit computes the exact digit sum whose parity determines whether the number is counted.
Invariant: For each candidate, the digit accumulator equals the sum of its processed decimal digits before its parity is tested.
Edge cases: The range starts at one and includes `num`; a single-digit number is handled by the same digit loop.
Complexity: O(num log num) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
code: class Solution { public int countEven(int num){int ans=0;for(int x=1;x<=num;x++){int n=x,sum=0;while(n>0){sum+=n%10;n/=10;}if(sum%2==0)ans++;}return ans;} }
complexity_reason: Extracting each decimal digit computes the exact digit sum whose parity determines whether the number is counted.

title: Counting Words With a Given Prefix
approach_name: Count startswith matches
notes:
Task and constraints: Count how many words start with the given prefix.
Idea: For every word, test `word.startswith(pref)` or compare its first `len(pref)` characters with `pref`, adding one for each match.
Technique and why it applies: A starts-with comparison tests the required initial substring without searching later positions.
Invariant: The count equals the number of processed words whose initial substring is exactly the requested prefix.
Edge cases: A word equal to the prefix qualifies; longer prefixes than a word do not match; repeated words count separately.
Complexity: O(total characters inspected) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
code:
class Solution:
 def prefixCount(self,words,pref):return sum(w.startswith(pref) for w in words)
complexity_reason: A starts-with comparison tests the required initial substring without searching later positions.

title: Cells in a Range on an Excel Sheet
approach_name: Enumerate columns then rows
notes:
Task and constraints: Return all cell names in the rectangular range from the first cell through the second, ordered by column then row.
Idea: Parse the start and end column letters and row digits, then enumerate columns outermost and rows innermost to build each cell name.
Technique and why it applies: Enumerating columns before rows yields the required Excel-cell ordering.
Invariant: The nested loops produce column-major order: all rows for one column precede the next column.
Edge cases: Both endpoints are included; the specified range uses single-letter columns and valid ascending row/column bounds.
Complexity: O(C·R) time and O(C·R) output space for C columns and R rows.
complexity_reason: Enumerating columns before rows yields the required Excel-cell ordering.

title: Cells in a Range on an Excel Sheet
approach_name: Enumerate columns then rows
notes:
Task and constraints: Return all cell names in the rectangular range from the first cell through the second, ordered by column then row.
Idea: Parse the start and end column letters and row digits, then enumerate columns outermost and rows innermost to build each cell name.
Technique and why it applies: Enumerating columns before rows yields the required Excel-cell ordering.
Invariant: The nested loops produce column-major order: all rows for one column precede the next column.
Edge cases: Both endpoints are included; the specified range uses single-letter columns and valid ascending row/column bounds.
Complexity: O(C·R) time and O(C·R) output space for C columns and R rows.
code:
import java.util.*;
class Solution { public List<String> cellsInRange(String s){String[] p=s.split(":");char c1=p[0].charAt(0),c2=p[1].charAt(0);int r1=Integer.parseInt(p[0].substring(1)),r2=Integer.parseInt(p[1].substring(1));List<String> out=new ArrayList<>();for(char c=c1;c<=c2;c++)for(int r=r1;r<=r2;r++)out.add(""+c+r);return out;} }
complexity_reason: Enumerating columns before rows yields the required Excel-cell ordering.

title: Find All K-Distant Indices in an Array
approach_name: Collect indices near any key occurrence
notes:
Task and constraints: Return all indices i for which some key index j satisfies abs(i-j)<=k, in increasing order.
Idea: Collect indices where `nums[j] == key`, then scan candidate indices in ascending order and include `i` if it lies within `k` of any key index; alternatively append clipped intervals and deduplicate in order if that is the code's approach.
Technique and why it applies: Checking distance to key occurrences includes every eligible index once and preserves increasing order.
Invariant: Every returned index is within distance `k` of at least one key occurrence, and scanning candidates in order keeps the result increasing.
Edge cases: An index near multiple key occurrences appears once; boundaries are clipped to `[0,n-1]`; if no key occurs, the result is empty.
Complexity: O(n²) for checking every index against every key index, or O(n+k·q) for interval expansion with q key occurrences; space is O(n).
complexity_reason: Checking distance to key occurrences includes every eligible index once and preserves increasing order.

title: Find All K-Distant Indices in an Array
approach_name: Collect indices near any key occurrence
notes:
Task and constraints: Return all indices i for which some key index j satisfies abs(i-j)<=k, in increasing order.
Idea: Collect indices where `nums[j] == key`, then scan candidate indices in ascending order and include `i` if it lies within `k` of any key index; alternatively append clipped intervals and deduplicate in order if that is the code's approach.
Technique and why it applies: Checking distance to key occurrences includes every eligible index once and preserves increasing order.
Invariant: Every returned index is within distance `k` of at least one key occurrence, and scanning candidates in order keeps the result increasing.
Edge cases: An index near multiple key occurrences appears once; boundaries are clipped to `[0,n-1]`; if no key occurs, the result is empty.
Complexity: O(n²) for checking every index against every key index, or O(n+k·q) for interval expansion with q key occurrences; space is O(n).
code:
import java.util.*;
class Solution { public List<Integer> findKDistantIndices(int[] nums,int key,int k){List<Integer> out=new ArrayList<>();for(int i=0;i<nums.length;i++){for(int j=Math.max(0,i-k);j<=Math.min(nums.length-1,i+k);j++)if(nums[j]==key){out.add(i);break;}}return out;} }
complexity_reason: Checking distance to key occurrences includes every eligible index once and preserves increasing order.
